stories.title: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
stories.originalTitle: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
stories.summary: Silent data corruption (SDC) happens when hardware, such as a GPU, returns a wrong but plausible number and raises no error. In distributed training, the wrong number can flow into the gradients and weights of every replica. Loss can still look normal for hour
points: Silent data corruption (SDC) happens when hardware, such as a GPU, returns a wrong but plausible number and raises no error.
In distributed training, the wrong number can flow into the gradients and weights of every replica.
Loss can still look normal for hours, and by the time a team notices an unexplained divergence or a weaker model, the compute is spent.

points: AI agents and applications that answer questions about recent events, product releases, prices, or regulations need information newer than their model’s training data.
Until now, Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore delivered that information to agents through AgentCore Gateway , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
That means creating a gateway and a web search target and calling the tool from an MCP client.
